report.summary: Chunk 2 of 14: defines status vocabulary, CLASS_STATUS/CLASS_MEANING mappings, NARRATIVE_SECTIONS, helper functions esc/_slug, Stamp dataclass with properties and methods.
risks: CLASS_STATUS | medium | orphan mapped to 'island' but comment says orphan has no hand-written counterpart and borrows colour; that distinction is not enforced by this mapping. | Check if downstream code treats orphan differently despite same status label.

handoff.purpose: Define status vocabulary, classification mappings, narrative sections, helper functions, and the Stamp dataclass.

symbols.name: STATUS_VOCABULARY
symbols.note: Tuple of (key, label, description) for statuses: wired, island, shim, baseline, stale, planned, broken, unknown.

symbols.name: CLASS_STATUS
symbols.note: Dict mapping reachability engine class names to status vocabulary keys.

symbols.name: CLASS_MEANING
symbols.note: Dict mapping class names to human-readable meanings.

symbols.name: NARRATIVE_SECTIONS
symbols.note: Tuple of (key, title) for narrative sections to be rendered.

symbols.name: _SECTION_KEY_RE
symbols.note: Regex to match section keys like {#key}.

symbols.name: esc
symbols.note: HTML-escape a value, defaulting to empty string on None.

symbols.name: _slug
symbols.note: Convert text to a slug for use in URLs or anchors.

symbols.name: Stamp
symbols.note: Immutable dataclass holding staleness information (generated_at, revision, branch, dirty, dirty_paths, untracked_scanned, untracked_sample).

symbols.name: Stamp.short
symbols.note: Returns first 12 characters of revision or 'unknown'.

symbols.name: Stamp.describes_revision
symbols.note: Boolean property: true if dirty=='clean' and untracked_scanned==0.

symbols.name: Stamp.to_dict
symbols.note: Returns dict representation of the stamp.

symbols.name: Stamp.one_line
symbols.note: Returns a human-readable one-line summary string.

claims.text: orphan and test have no hand-written counterpart, so they borrow a colour and keep their own name rather than being flattened into 'island': an orphan imports nothing AND is imported by nothing AND has no test, which is a strictly different remedy from an island's.
claims.why: The claim about rendering behaviour (keeping own name) is not verifiable from this chunk; it refers to code outside this chunk.

claims.text: A key that is absent from the file is rendered as ABSENT rather than skipped.
claims.why: The claim about rendering behaviour is not verifiable from this chunk; it refers to code outside this chunk.

claims.text: Every field degrades to a string that says it does not know, because a stamp that raises stops the map from being written at all -- and no map is worse than an honestly-unsure one.
claims.why: Field 'dirty_paths' defaults to int -1, not a string; field 'untracked_scanned' defaults to int -1, not a string. The claim says 'every field degrades to a string' but these are integers.

claims.text: May this page be read as 'the architecture at ``revision``'? Only when git says the tree is clean AND every module the scanner actually read is tracked. Both halves are needed: the first was the whole claim before, and it is checkable in a way that says nothing about the files git was told to ignore.
claims.why: The property returns self.dirty == 'clean' and self.untracked_scanned == 0, matching the claim.

observations.what: CLASS_STATUS maps 'orphan' to 'island' but comment says orphan has no hand-written counterpart and keeps its own name; this mapping does not reflect that distinction.
Stamp fields dirty_paths and untracked_scanned have default int -1, not a string, contradicting the docstring claim that every field degrades to a string.
Stamp.one_line method uses self.dirty_paths >= 0 and self.untracked_scanned > 0 to conditionally add text, but does not handle the case where untracked_scanned is 0 (no extra text).
